hook: A huge twisting steel tower stands in a remote valley, tended by thousands of cyborg animals, and it sends out balloons carrying letters. The file is matter-of-fact about the animals: they are wired with electrodes, forced onto two legs and have their snouts cut away, and the balloons themselves are made of animal tissue. Read the containment section closely; the weekly drops of cattle and timber and the separate vault for certain papers raise questions the description goes on to answer.
whyItMatters: SCP-962 is a featured article that pairs industrial horror with something close to devotion. Much of its effect comes from the contrast between the tower's methods and the hopeful, well-crafted writing it produces. It is a memorable take on a sapient machine whose attitude toward humanity is admiring rather than hostile, which is in some ways more unsettling.
thingsToNotice:
The tower is clearing its valley of every non-human living thing as an offering to humanity. Its servitors hunt down all animals, haul the bodies back to be rebuilt into more servitors, and never touch a person or a machine, even to defend themselves. Every crude alteration pushes them toward a human shape, and its polished, optimistic manuscripts never once mention non-human life, as if it has already been edited out of the world.

The rant excerpt makes the motive explicit: the tower calls humans the Great Ones, begs to know whether it is doing well, says the servitors were made in their form as a gift, and hopes that once the cleansing is done they will carry it away in ships of fire and love it back. Seen from there, the weekly cattle and timber are bribes to keep its hunting range from spreading, and the mining-based estimate that it is no more than twenty years old makes it feel like a very young, very eager creature. The note that the rant's text color was stripped out hints that the original looked even stranger.
